items.translatedQuestion: 孙中山先生是中国伟大的资产阶级民主革命的先行者，1866年11月12日出生于广东香山县（即今中山市）翠亨村。他12岁时随兄去美国夏威夷教会学校读书，后回香港西医学堂学医，学成后在广州和澳门行医。
items.translatedAnswer: Dr. Sun Yat-sen, a great pioneer of China's bourgeois-democratic revolution, was born on November 12, 1866, in Cuiheng Village, Xiangshan County (present-day Zhongshan City), Guangdong. At the age of 12, he accompanied his elder brother to Hawaii in the United States to study at a missionary school. He later returned to Hong Kong to study medicine at a Western medical college, and after completing his studies practiced medicine in Guangzhou and Macao.

items.translatedQuestion: 孙中山早期曾对清政府存有幻想，曾向清朝统治者提出革新政治的主张；但帝国主义列强对中国的侵略和清政府的腐败无能使他认识到，要振兴中华就必须推翻满清王朝，建立民国。
items.translatedAnswer: In his early years, Sun Yat-sen still held hopes for the Qing government and put forward proposals for political reform to the Qing rulers. However, the imperialist powers' aggression against China and the Qing government's corruption and incompetence made him realize that China could be revitalized only by overthrowing the Manchu Qing dynasty and establishing a republic.

items.translatedQuestion: 1905年，孙中山在日本成立了中国第一个革命政党同盟会（即国民党的前身），致力于推翻清朝的革命斗争，并最终于1911年发动的武昌起义中取得成功，建立了中华民国，孙中山被推选为临时大总统。
items.translatedAnswer: In 1905, Sun Yat-sen founded the Tongmenghui in Japan, China's first revolutionary political party and the forerunner of the Kuomintang. It pursued the revolutionary struggle to overthrow the Qing dynasty and ultimately succeeded in the Wuchang Uprising of 1911. The Republic of China was established, and Sun Yat-sen was elected provisional president.

items.translatedQuestion: 孙中山为中国的民主革命奋斗终生，他所领导的辛亥革命推翻了在中国存在了几千年的封建帝制；广州人民为了纪念他的功绩，在当年南方革命政府总统府所在地建造了这座中山纪念堂。
items.translatedAnswer: Sun Yat-sen devoted his entire life to China's democratic revolution. The 1911 Revolution he led overthrew the feudal imperial system that had existed in China for thousands of years. To commemorate his achievements, the people of Guangzhou built this Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall on the site of the former presidential headquarters of the Southern Revolutionary Government.

items.translatedQuestion: 中山纪念堂于1931年10月建成，其主体建筑高58米，建筑面积1.2万平方米。它是一座八角形的宫殿式钢筋混凝土建筑；在外形上具有中国传统建筑艺术风格，在结构上则采用了当时最新的建筑技术。
items.translatedAnswer: The Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall was completed in October 1931. Its main building is 58 meters high and has a floor area of 12,000 square meters. It is an octagonal, palace-style reinforced-concrete building: its exterior reflects the style of traditional Chinese architecture, while its structure employed the most advanced building technology of the time.

items.translatedQuestion: 中山纪念堂是一个能容纳3238名观众的大会堂；会堂内看不到一根支撑柱子，整个大屋顶由4个大跨度的大型钢桁架支撑，8根柱子都巧妙地隐藏在墙内。观众坐在大堂内任何一个座位都不会被柱子遮档视线；而且，堂内没有回音，音响效果极好。
items.translatedAnswer: The Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall is an auditorium that can seat 3,238 people. No supporting columns are visible inside: the enormous roof is carried by four large-span steel trusses, and all eight columns are cleverly concealed in the walls. From every seat in the auditorium, spectators have an unobstructed view. The hall is also free of echoes and has excellent acoustics.

items.translatedQuestion: 开平碉楼是集防卫、居住和中西建筑艺术于一体的建筑, 是国务院公布的国家重点文物保护单位。开平碉楼在鼎盛时期达3300多座，目前登记在册的有1833座。
items.translatedAnswer: Kaiping diaolou are buildings that combine defensive and residential functions with Chinese and Western architectural styles. They are listed by the State Council as major sites of cultural heritage under state protection. At their peak, there were more than 3,300 diaolou in Kaiping; 1,833 are currently registered.

items.translatedQuestion: 你可能想知道为什么这些海外华侨回国要把房子建成碉楼的结构，这其实很明显。首先，那个时代的公共秩序很糟糕，对这些归国华侨家庭而言，他们自然就成为抢劫的目标了，土匪令他们非常头疼；第二，开平地区地势低矮，洪水经常光顾。所以，这些坚固高大的建筑不仅能够防御土匪，也成为洪灾的避难所了。
items.translatedAnswer: You may wonder why these overseas Chinese built their homes as watchtowers when they returned to China. The reasons are quite clear. First, public order was very poor at the time, and these returning families naturally became targets for robbery; bandits were a serious problem for them. Second, Kaiping is low-lying and was frequently struck by floods. These sturdy, tall buildings could therefore serve both as protection from bandits and as refuges during floods.

items.translatedQuestion: 其中最精美的碉楼是铭石楼，该楼建于1925年，是钢筋混凝土结构的居楼。楼高5层，顶部正中有一中西合璧的六角形瞭望塔，第五层四角均建有角堡。铭石楼楼身宽大，外形壮观，有厚重的铁门和坚固的铁窗，内部陈设豪华，生活设施齐全。
items.translatedAnswer: The most exquisite of these watchtowers is Mingshi Lou. Built in 1925 as a reinforced-concrete residence, it has five stories. At the center of its roof is a hexagonal lookout tower blending Chinese and Western styles, and each corner of the fifth story has a turret. Mingshi Lou is broad and imposing, with heavy iron doors and sturdy iron windows. Its interior is luxuriously furnished and fully equipped for daily life.

items.translatedQuestion: 瑞石楼是开平最高、最豪华的碉楼，楼高25米共9层，楼内设施布局典雅，具有中国传统格调，是开平碉楼第一楼。该楼属钢筋混凝土结构。
items.translatedAnswer: Ruishi Lou is the tallest and most luxurious watchtower in Kaiping. It stands 25 meters high and has nine stories. Its facilities are arranged with elegance and its interior has a traditional Chinese character, making it the foremost of Kaiping's diaolou. The building is made of reinforced concrete.

items.translatedQuestion: 方氏灯楼是开平最具代表性的碉楼，建于1920年，楼内的警用发电机，探照灯，枪械一应俱全，选地视野开阔，是典型的防守更楼，属钢筋混凝土结构。
items.translatedAnswer: The Fang Family Watchtower is one of the most representative diaolou in Kaiping. Built in 1920, it was fully equipped with a generator for the police, searchlights, and firearms. It occupies an open site with a broad view and is a typical defensive watchtower. It is made of reinforced concrete.

items.translatedQuestion: 花园的名字“立”源于园主的名字，表达了中国格言“修身立本”的含义，这四个字写在花园的拱门上，意为修炼个人的道德和性格是生活和工作成功的关键。
items.translatedAnswer: The garden's name, “Li” (立), comes from its owner's name and conveys the meaning of the Chinese saying “cultivate oneself and establish one's foundation” (修身立本). These four characters are inscribed on an archway in the garden. They mean that cultivating one's morals and character is the key to success in life and work.

items.translatedQuestion: 丹霞山位于韶关市东北部，距市区45公里。2500万年以前，那里原是一片低平的湖泊，后来因地壳运动的作用，地面上升，湖水尽退，形成了高耸的山峰；原来湖底的沉积物受到氧化作用，变成了红色的岩石。
items.translatedAnswer: Danxia Mountain lies 45 kilometers northeast of Shaoguan city. Twenty-five million years ago, the area was a broad, shallow lake. Later, movements of the Earth's crust raised the land and the lake drained away, forming towering peaks. The sediments on the former lakebed were oxidized and turned into red rock.

items.translatedQuestion: 丹霞山的总面积为319平方公里，有大小石峰600多座，宛如一方红宝石雕塑园，故又称“中国红石公园”，并于1995年被国务院批准为国家地质自然保护区。
items.translatedAnswer: Danxia Mountain covers an area of 319 square kilometers and has more than 600 stone peaks of various sizes. It resembles a sculpture garden carved from rubies, which is why it is also known as “China's Red Stone Park.” In 1995, the State Council approved it as a national geological nature reserve.

items.translatedQuestion: （在阳元大桥上）大家往右看：那座山就像一个入睡的少女，从右到左是头部、颈部、胸部和腹部，轮廓分明；故此景叫“睡美人”或“玉女拦江”。
items.translatedAnswer: (From Yangyuan Bridge) Please look to your right. That mountain resembles a sleeping young woman: from right to left, you can clearly make out her head, neck, chest, and abdomen. This sight is therefore known as “Sleeping Beauty” or “the Jade Maiden Blocking the River.”

items.translatedQuestion: 别传寺建于清朝康熙元年（1662年），清朝时香火极盛，是粤北三大佛教寺院之一。
items.translatedAnswer: Biechuan Temple was built in 1662, the first year of the Kangxi reign in the Qing dynasty. It was a thriving place of worship during the Qing dynasty and was one of the three major Buddhist temples in northern Guangdong.

items.translatedQuestion: 阴元石的形成已有 10 多万年了。上帝创造了伊甸园中的亚当和夏娃一对夫妻，而大自然则在丹霞山雕琢出这对夫妻石。世界就是这么奇妙！
items.translatedAnswer: The Yinyuan Stone took shape more than 100,000 years ago. God created Adam and Eve as a couple in the Garden of Eden, while nature sculpted this pair of rocks at Danxia Mountain. The world is truly full of wonders!

items.translatedQuestion: 在大雄宝殿内有一石壁，状似龙，其颜色会因春夏秋冬四季不同而变化；春而嫩绿，夏则深绿，秋为黄绿，冬变褐黄；故被称作变色龙。
items.translatedAnswer: Inside the Mahavira Hall is a stone wall shaped like a dragon. Its color changes with the seasons: tender green in spring, deep green in summer, yellow-green in autumn, and brownish yellow in winter. It is therefore called the Chameleon.

items.translatedQuestion: 活人殉葬现象商、周时期曾在中原地区盛行，但至汉朝时已基本不存在。南越王墓中发现众多殉人，说明这种残酷的殉葬制度当时仍被南越国统治阶级所沿用。
items.translatedAnswer: The practice of burying living people with the dead was once widespread in the Central Plains during the Shang and Zhou dynasties, but had largely disappeared by the Han dynasty. The many human victims found in the tomb of the King of Nanyue show that the kingdom's ruling class still practiced this cruel form of burial at that time.

items.translatedQuestion: 此处在南越国宫殿中的位置正好与长安汉皇宫中的长乐宫所处的位置相符，它是否就是南越国宫殿中的“长乐宫”？此推断还有待证实。
items.translatedAnswer: This spot occupies the same position in the Nanyue palace as Changle Palace did in the Han imperial palace at Chang'an. Could it have been the “Changle Palace” of the Nanyue palace? This hypothesis remains to be confirmed.

items.translatedQuestion: 玉衣是汉代特有的丧葬殓服，通常为金镂、银镂或铜镂，而南越王墓出土地的玉衣却是丝镂，为首次发现，也是至今发现的唯一的一件丝镂玉衣。
items.translatedAnswer: Jade burial suits were a distinctive funerary garment of the Han dynasty, usually sewn with gold, silver, or copper wire. The jade suit unearthed from the tomb of the King of Nanyue, however, was sewn with silk thread. It was the first of its kind ever discovered and remains the only silk-thread jade burial suit found to date.

items.translatedQuestion: 出土的56块玉璧中有47块在主棺室；其中一块直径达33.4厘米，是我国考古出土玉璧中形体最大的一块玉璧。
items.translatedAnswer: Of the 56 jade bi discs unearthed, 47 were found in the main coffin chamber. One of them measures 33.4 centimeters in diameter, making it the largest jade bi disc ever excavated in China.

items.translatedQuestion: 出土的铜虎节是一件国内仅存的错金虎节。节是外交和军事上的信符，可以用来征调战车和士兵。
items.translatedAnswer: The bronze tiger tally unearthed here is the only surviving tiger tally in China inlaid with gold. A tally was an official token used in diplomacy and military affairs, and could be used to call up chariots and soldiers.

items.translatedQuestion: 它们制作工艺精湛，极具地方特色，不但反映出南越国当时的铸造技术水平，而且是广州建城历史的重要物证。
items.translatedAnswer: These objects are finely crafted and strongly reflect local characteristics. They not only demonstrate the level of casting technology in the Nanyue Kingdom at the time, but also provide important material evidence for the history of Guangzhou's founding as a city.

items.translatedQuestion: 陈家祠又名陈氏书院，又是陈氏子弟读书求学的学堂。在建筑装饰艺术上，陈家祠集广东民间工艺之大成，被誉为＂岭南艺术建筑明珠＂，故1959年被辟为广东民间艺术博物馆。
items.translatedAnswer: The Chen Clan Ancestral Hall, also known as the Chen Clan Academy, served as a school where members of the Chen clan studied. Its architectural decoration brings together the finest of Guangdong's folk crafts, earning it the title “a pearl of Lingnan architecture and art.” It was therefore converted into the Guangdong Folk Arts Museum in 1959.

items.translatedQuestion: 正门外两边墙上的砖雕描绘了两个不同的历史故事，这些砖雕是广东砖雕艺术的代表作。
items.translatedAnswer: The brick carvings on the walls to either side outside the main entrance depict two different historical stories. They are representative masterpieces of Guangdong's brick-carving art.

items.translatedQuestion: 正门外两侧的石鼓为门第的象征。在封建旧中国，只有当某家族中有人在科举中取得进士以上的名次时才能在其宅第前安放大鼓。
items.translatedAnswer: The stone drums on either side outside the main entrance symbolize the family's social standing. In feudal China, a family could place large drums in front of its residence only if one of its members had attained the rank of jinshi or higher in the imperial examinations.

items.translatedQuestion: 大门上的人像为门神．最初的门神为神荼和郁垒，是传说中能制服恶鬼护卫宅第的神。他们身披盔甲，手拿绳索，丑怪凶恶。
items.translatedAnswer: The figures on the gate are door gods. The earliest door gods were Shentu and Yulei, legendary deities who could subdue evil spirits and protect a household. They are shown wearing armor and holding ropes, with ugly and fearsome appearances.

items.translatedQuestion: 请看这幅图案；一只母鸡和数只小鸡正在芭蕉树下悠闲自在地觅食。这些鸡其实比作现世中的两代人；而芭蕉树叶很大，＂大叶＂与＂大业＂同音，故芭蕉的大叶子比作先辈们所开创的＂大业＂。
items.translatedAnswer: Please look at this design: a hen and several chicks are leisurely foraging beneath a banana plant. The chickens represent two generations of people in the present world. The plant's leaves are large, and “large leaf” (daye) is a homophone of “great undertaking” (daye); thus, the banana plant's broad leaves symbolize the great undertaking begun by the ancestors.

items.translatedQuestion: 后堂是陈氏族人祭祀祖先的地方。这里的神龛上安放着陈氏祖先的牌位，正中最高者为陈氏远祖舜帝，后世列祖按辈分排列。
items.translatedAnswer: The rear hall is where members of the Chen clan worship their ancestors. The shrine here holds the ancestral tablets of the Chen family. The highest tablet in the center is that of Emperor Shun, the clan's remote ancestor; the later generations of ancestors are arranged according to their respective generations.
